title: I made EVERWHEN: text a message to anyone in history, then a D20 + AI mechanics decide how the timeline changes
author: Competitive_Set2787
selftext:
**Game Title:** Everwhen  
**Playable Link:** [https://playeverwhen.com](https://playeverwhen.com/)  
**Platform:** Browser  
**Description:** An indie time-based RPG. You pick a goal (say, stop a war), write a short message, 160 characters, to any historical figure in any year, and then a D20 roll plus an AI resolve what actually happens. Five messages per run, and it writes the aftermath back to you as a unique chronicle. Sometimes your advice lands. Sometimes the dice betray you and you make things much much worse. It is legitimately a game that could not have existed without AI game mechanics, so in my opinion it is refreshingly new. Feedback very much welcome, this is my first game and I'm nervous about showing the world. 🤞  
**Free to Play Status:**

* First run is free
* 100% off for first 100 redemptions, code: **ALPHA100**
* Up to 30 free plays via referrals

**Involvement:** Solo developer

comments.author: Time_Cat_5212
comments.body: Amazing idea!  Immediately into it.  Having fun playing it.  Not just another "I created a game from 2000 using Fable"

replies.author: Competitive_Set2787
replies.body:
Thanks!

Fable was definitely involved in my build 🫣 but this still took me 2 months of iteration to get the mechanics feeling right.

Hope you enjoy it, always open to feedback.

replies.author: Time_Cat_5212
replies.body: Seems to me the gameplay is based heavily on factual reference and reading comprehension which IMO is a good angle.  It also seems flexible enough to turn a silly idea into a real one if you fold in enough facts.  Love it!

comments.author: London2022
comments.body: Do you have to pay the API AI generation fees anytime someone tries it?

replies.author: Competitive_Set2787
replies.body:
Unfortunately yes, but I consider just cost of acquisition.

If the game ever took off I’d probably just buy a DGX Spark or something so that it was a one time fixed cost. Could also lower costs for users too.

Currently I’m using Anthropic models which excel at this sort of writing and reasoning, I haven’t had as much quality and success when I swap out open models yet.

replies.author: London2022
replies.body:
Thanks for reply man  
  
Oh interesting; didnt know what the DGX Sparks was. I suppose with the rate of model growth, in 2 or less years a model just for speech and response in certain environments would be extremely cost effective (maybe even run at the local hardware levle) 

So many ideas - thought yours was really fun. I was interested as wanted to see if NPC AI fuid chat was possible.

Your game is a fun idea - I tried to write to Henry VIII but they executed me for calling him mate haha. I shared it with a housemate who also enjoyed it.
